text:
alice: heads-up — CI is flagging a couple of recent model admissions: ONNX export fails intermittently and benchmark numbers diverge vs the HF baseline. need a quick follow-up to lock down gating + long-term design for the pipeline.

alice: repro steps are here — model X (hf:llama-x) -> export (torch->onnx) -> quantize -> run bench. export sometimes succeeds but with wrong dynamic_axes, which then makes runtime kernels misbehave.

dmitri: saw that. export logs show `ValueError: dynamic_axes mismatch` for 2 models. also tokenizer vocab size mismatch for one of them. suspect preprocessing metadata is missing from the model bundle.

carmen: +1. we need two orthogonal gates: (1) fast compatibility/sanity checks (export + shape/tokenizer) and (2) full correctness/bench. fast gate should run in ~10m on CPU or cheap GPU. full bench can be async and scheduled.

ben: what's failing in the bench? is it latency only or output quality?

alice: both. latency p95/p99 are worse for the onnx path in some cases (kernel selection picking suboptimal kernels because sequence length dims were wrong). quality: embeddings drifted — cosine similarity vs HF < 0.995 for a small set of probe prompts.

eval-bot: automated-eval: model X: embedding_cosine=0.988 (threshold 0.995) | p95_latency=210ms (target 150ms) | kl_divergence=0.012 (threshold 0.01)

dmitri: those thresholds are the key tradeoff. we shouldn't be overly strict for first pass; but if embedding_cosine < 0.98 we should auto-reject. between 0.98-0.995 -> require human review.

carmen: proposing concrete design:
- Stage 0 (ingest): validate model card + manifest fields (vocab_hash, tokenizer_class, dynamic_axes_hint, framework_version). reject if manifest missing required keys.
- Stage 1 (smoke export): attempt export with standardized exporter container. record exporter metadata (exporter_version, opset, dynamic_axes). fail early on export/shape errors. target time < 10m.
- Stage 2 (compat check): run quick inference with a set of short+long prompts (CPU or small GPU) to assert tensor shapes, KV cache behavior, and deterministic outputs for same seed. check tokenization roundtrip.
- Stage 3 (bench + quality): run full bench on representative load profile (mix of seq lengths), compute p50/p95/p99, throughput, embedding cosine, KL on logit categories, output-surface tests. can be async; gating based on thresholds.

carmen: plus: capture normalized reference outputs on HF CPU/GPU and compare with our runtime. thresholds: embedding_cosine >= 0.995 pass, 0.98-0.995 review, <0.98 reject. logit_kl < 0.01 pass. latency thresholds per model-class (small/med/large) stored in model class config.

ben: sounds good. how do we avoid paying GPU time for every PR/variant?

alice: two cost controls: (A) cheap smoke on ingest to fail fast (CPU or tiny GPU), (B) sample-based full bench — only run full bench on the first admission of a model family/version or when smoke indicates high risk (tokenizer mismatch, export warning), and (C) a queued cadence: full benches run nightly if not urgent.

infra-bot: note: we have 6 reserved GPUs for admission-jobs. current queue avg wait 14m.

carmen: interface boundaries: exporter should return a single json metadata blob: `export_meta.json` with keys: `framework`, `ops_version`, `dynamic_axes`, `vocab_hash`, `layernorm_eps`, `float_mode` (fp32/16/int8), `kv_layout` (packed/unpacked). admission service uses that blob to decide kernel selection and quantization profiles.

alice: agree. also add an admission API schema that requires: `manifest.version`, `manifest.model_class`, `export_meta.hash`, `ref_metrics` (optional). If missing ref_metrics then bench will compute and populate them.

ben: what about quantized vs non-quantized pipelines? exporter might produce both. we should run smoke on both but full bench on the variant we intend to serve (e.g., int8).

dmitri: important: tokenizer mismatch root cause — some HF repos use `tokenizer.json` + merges; others rely on slow Python-only tokenizer. admission should run a tokenization roundtrip test: encode->decode->encode and confirm ids identical. fail if >0.5% mismatch.

carmen: for long-term refactor: move the heavy benching out of the monolith into an async microservice (model-admit-worker) that consumes events, runs bench jobs on the GPU cluster, and reports results back via event stream. admission service only performs fast checks and orchestration.

alice: agree, plus add a human review queue for borderline models (metrics in review window). add a small UI in Console to inspect failed diffs: diff of normalized outputs, kernel selection logs, and tokenization mismatches.

eval-bot: suggestion: add a deterministic synthetic workload generator that seeds sequences of tokens sampled from production input histograms. we can replay real-ish load without hitting customer data.

ben: how to define "normalized outputs"? for logits we should softmax then maybe top-K distribution compare. for generative text we can use ngram overlap + perplexity. store both HF-ref and our runtime ref.

carmen: implementation notes:
- exporter container: pinned torch/onnxruntime versions, unit tests for dynamic_axes heuristics.
- admission job matrix: {exporter, quant_profile, runtime_image, seq_lengths=[8,64,512], batch_sizes=[1,4]}
- cost-control: early bailouts and sample-based suites.

alice: action items:
- dmitri: add tokenizer roundtrip check to Stage 1 smoke (owner) — due EOD tomorrow.
- ben: draft export_meta schema + example — due Wed.
- carmen: prototype admission event schema and worker sketch — due Fri.
- infra: (infra-bot) please increase admission GPU pool if possible or give ETA on queue reduction.

dmitri: noted. I'll open a tiny PR to run tokenizer roundtrip in the exporter container and add a failing test case.

ben: I'll post an example `export_meta.json` in #eng-ml and link to the small schema in the repo.

infra-bot: ops-note: exploring adding 2 GPUs to the admission pool next week, will update.

alice: thanks all. want to sync briefly tomorrow 10am to finalize thresholds and decide which checks are mandatory vs advisory.

carmen: +1. I'll add a short RFC doc with the stages and thresholds and link it here. :thumbsup:

ben: one last thought — we should version gate exporter behavior (exporter_v1 vs v2) so we can evolve heuristics without breaking existing admitted models.

alice: good call. add exporter_version to export_meta and admission decisions can include allowed exporter versions per model class.

eval-bot: automated-eval: queued full bench for model X (job 482)

alice: perfect — we'll triage results once that job finishes.

ben: thanks everyone, good progress.
